The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- with interest for the Ashwathappa A.P vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 18 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60732771/
1 injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident.
2. The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 23.10.2021 at about 10.00 pm., when the petitioner was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 from Vokkaligara Samudhaya Bhavana S.S.Ghati Tobagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk near Happy Valley resorts, the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side but fell down.

sentences.text: Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital Doddaballapura wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for 6 days and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards his treatment and nourishment.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was SCCH - 9 3 MVC No.460/2022 doing agriculturist work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

The accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B- 9051 by its driver and the jurisdictional Doddaballapura Rural police have registered a case in their crime No.287/2021, after investigation the said police have filed a charge sheet against the said driver,
punishable under Section 279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC.

The first respondent being the insurer and the second respondent being the policy holder of said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- under all heads together with interest and costs.

3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and have filed their respective written statement.
4.
The brief contentions of the written statement of SCCH - 9 4 MVC No.460/2022 respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner.

Respondent contended that,
compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Further denied the involvement of Bus bearing No.KA-06-B-9051 in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, driver of the Bus was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further contended that, the said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-060B-9051 was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

Further the respondent No.1 has contended that, the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and Ashwathappa A.P vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 18 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60732771/
2 158(6) of M.V.Act.

sentences.text: Respondent admitted the issuance of policy of insurance in favour of second respondent in respect of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, on all these SCCH - 9 5 MVC No.460/2022 contentions, the respondent No.1 prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner.

Further contended that, he is the RC owner of Bus bearing No.KA-06-B-9051, the RTO and such other documents pertaining to the said bus are standing in his name, the same was insured with the 1st respondent and the said policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner prove that on 23.10.2022 at about 10.00 pm., SCCH - 9 6 M V C N o . 4 6 0 / 2 0 2 2 t h e p e t i t i o n e r w a s t r a v e l l i n g i n a b u s b e a r i n g reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 in order to attend marriage reception and after completion of reception while returning back in the same bus near Valley Resorts, S.S.Ghati,
Makalidurga Road, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time, the driver of the bus in which he was travelling drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly dahed to the road safety guard at right side bus fell down.
Due to impact the petitioner and other inmates of the said bus sustained grievous injuries in the alleged RTA ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked the 8 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.
P.9. On the other hand, to prove the defenses forthcoming in the objection, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence, for consideration.

7. Heard.
8.

Issue No.1:

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.1:

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 23.10.2021 at about 10.00 pm., when he was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 from Vokkaligara Samudhaya Bhavana S.S.Ghati Tobagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk near Happy Valley resorts, the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dahed to the road safety guard at right side but fell down.
Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries.
As a result he sustained injuries.

10. To prove the accident that occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending bus, the petitioner himself got examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.

On perusal of police document i.e., Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the charge heet, Ex.P.4 is the spot panchanama, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the sketch, Ex.P.7 is the SCCH - 9 8 MVC No.460/2022 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the out patient slip and Ex.P.9 is the Aadhar card.

11. On perusal of documents, police have investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 as per Ex.P.3 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338, 304(a) of IPC.
On perusal of said documents the owner and driver of the offending Bus have not disputed involvement of vehicles.
The respondent No.1 counsel suggested to the PW-1 that the said private bus was not having permit.

Therefore, by considering the oral and documentary evidence on record and above discussion, I am of the opinion that, the accident was occurred on negligence of driver of the offending Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051.
The petitioner has produced out patient book as per Ex.P.8, that document discloses the petitioner has sustained injury.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into SCCH - 9 9 MVC No.460/2022 several facts like injuries, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant, charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one.
13.
In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, examination in chief during the evidence, produced his out patient book marked at Ex.P8.
The said document discloses that, he had sustained injury.
Petitioner has not produced discharge summary as well as medical bills.

sentences.text: Subsequently, the petitioner remained as silent spectator without appearing before the court, to prove further points with respect to his pain and sufferings and actual laid up and rest period taken by his for treatment and also not appeared to answer, what the specific amount he had spent for his food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Another point to be added to this, in connection with the earnings, as well as disability of the petitioner SCCH - 9 10 MVC No.460/2022 consequent upon the accident, has not made an effort to examine the doctor for consideration.

15. All these lacuna and the silence on the part of the petitioner and failure on his part to participate effectively in the case on hand during the course of trial, makes this court to come to the conclusion that, the petitioner has utterly failed to prove the above issue, in order to get compensation amount claimed by the petitioner on different heads.
As already noted above, when the witness failed to tender for cross examination, his evidence is not trustworthy, it has to be discarded/ expunged.
16. In the light of my detailed discussion held above, the petitioner herein, has not made out the reliable and acceptable evidence to get the reliefs sought for in the case on hand.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Negative.
17. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
SCCH - 9 11 MVC No.460/2022 Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, no order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
